newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street firm at midday as tech stocks lead.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street firm at midday as tech stocks lead.

text.p: U.S. stocks were strong at midday on Wednesday, as the bond market recovered from recent losses and technology shares surged after Microsoft Corp said it would invest in Apple Computer Inc.
The Dow industrials, which have struggled recently as interest rates crept higher, gained ground on Wednesday as bond yields fell.
The blue-chip average was up 55 points, or 0.68 percent, at 8243, while the long bond gained 4/32 to yield 6.48 percent.
But the Dow turned around as bonds erased losses ahead of a closely watched Treasury auction of $12 billion in 10-year notes and the release of the Federal Reserve Beige Book data.
"Today appears to be more of catchup day for the Dow, which had been struggling lately," Greg Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities, said.
Most analysts had not expected the bond market to recover until after Thursday, when the Treasury was scheduled to sell $10 billion in 30-year bonds, Johnson said.
"The bond market rebound is coming a little earlier than expected, which is very good news," he said.
Microsoft's announcement of a $150 million investment in Apple also added fire to the technology sector and the broader stock market, analysts said.
"The technology market was looking for an excuse to rally and the excitement around Apple gave traders that excuse," Frank Calta, managing director of institutional trading at Dain Bosworth said.
Apple's stock soared 6-1/2 to 26-1/4 in active trade. The company also announced a broad series of alliances with Microsoft, as well as the replacement of all but two of its directors.
"The Apple news is simply really exciting," Johnson said.
Among other active issues, ITT Corp stock rose 1-15/16 to 64-7/8 after Hilton Hotels Corp said it increased its hostile bid for the company to $70 per share.
ITT said it would consider the new takeover offer "in due course." Hilton shares dropped 15/16 to 31-13/16.

Shares of Cisco Systems Inc lost 1-12/16 to 80-3/16 in brisk trade, after it posted fiscal fourth-quarter results that met Wall Street forecasts but fell short of the so-called "whisper" number, or unpublished estimates.
